age.evidence: A total of 96 male and female adult Wistar rats (Rattus norvegicus, 90 days old ...

sex.evidence: A total of 96 male and female adult Wistar rats (Rattus norvegicus, 90 days old, male n = 48 ... females n = 48 ...)

dosing.doses_raw: 2 mL/kg; approximately 10.62 mg/kg total alkaloids in rats (DMT 2.72 mg/kg, harmine 3.98 mg/kg, harmaline 0.20 mg/kg, tetrahydroharmine 3.72 mg/kg)
dosing.evidence: At 90 days old, rats were given an intragastric dose of Ayahuasca by oral gavage ... Control rats received water through intragastric gavage at the same dose (2 mL/kg). A single acute administration was employed.

group_housing.evidence: After weaning on postnatal day 21, the pups were housed in groups of 4 per cage.

day_night_flipped.evidence: Animals were kept in a 12-hour light-dark cycle at 22 ± 1 °C (direction / lights-on time not stated).

assays.assay_description: 5-min EPM (2 open arms 50 × 10 cm, 2 closed arms 50 × 10 × 40 cm, 5 × 5 cm central platform) under red light, 10 days after a single oral ayahuasca dose in control and maternally deprived rats. Time and entries in open and closed arms were measured.

application_type.evidence: rats were given an intragastric dose of Ayahuasca by oral gavage

setup_habituation.evidence: not reported; animals were placed on the central platform and allowed 5 min to explore

setup_restrain.evidence: The animals were placed on the central platform and allowed 5 min to explore the apparatus.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in EPM apparatus; home-cage chow ad libitum

water_restriction.evidence: No water in EPM apparatus; home-cage water ad libitum

time_to_assay.evidence: The elevated plus maze was performed 10 days after Ayahuasca administration.

sample_size.evidence: N = 24/group ... For Fig. 2A: Control+Water: N = 21; MD+Water: N = 20; Control + Aya: N = 19; MD + Aya: N = 19.

outcomes.summary: Maternal deprivation reduced open-arm time and increased closed-arm time. A single ayahuasca dose reversed both effects in MD rats. Open-arm entries were unaffected. Closed-arm entries were higher in MD+Aya rats. No Sex × Treatment interaction was found.
outcomes.statistics: Open-arm time: Treatment F(1,75)=20.76, P<0.0001; MD F(1,75)=11.38, P=0.0012; Interaction F(1,75)=6.713, P=0.0115; MD+Water vs MD+Aya P<0.0001. Closed-arm time: Treatment F(1,90)=13.38, P=0.0004; MD F(1,90)=14.18, P=0.0003; Interaction F(1,90)=4.46, P=0.0375; MD+Aya vs MD+Water P=0.0007. Open-arm entries: Interaction F(1,90)=0.1009, P=0.7515. Closed-arm entries: Treatment F(1,91)=6.585, P=0.0119; MD F(1,91)=4.149, P=0.0446.
outcomes.evidence: Ayahuasca treatment reversed this effect in the Maternal Deprivation group (P < 0.0001).

B1_num_measures.evidence: The parameters measured include the number of entries and the time spent in the open and closed arms (4 measures reported in results).

B6_cognitive.evidence: Innate conflict between exploration and aversion to open spaces.

E1_environment_type.evidence: 2 open arms (50 × 10 cm) and 2 closed arms (50 × 10 × 40 cm) arranged at right angles

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are not a shelter per rubric.

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM arms are not distinct compartments per rubric.

E7_social_context.evidence: The animals were placed on the central platform (individual testing).

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in apparatus.

D1_continuity.evidence: allowed 5 min to explore the apparatus

D3_recording_days.evidence: performed 10 days after Ayahuasca administration (single day)

D5_followup.evidence: The elevated plus maze was performed 10 days after Ayahuasca administration.

assays.assay_description: 5-min open field (40 × 60 cm, 50-cm walls, floor divided into 9 squares), 11 days after a single oral ayahuasca dose. Square crossings and rearings were scored in real time by an observer.

application_type.evidence: intragastric dose of Ayahuasca by oral gavage

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to explore the space freely for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food in open field; home-cage chow ad libitum

water_restriction.evidence: No water in open field; home-cage water ad libitum

time_to_assay.evidence: The open field test was performed 11 days after Ayahuasca administration.

sample_size.evidence: For Fig. 3A: Control+Water: N = 23; MD+Water: N = 24; Control + Aya: N = 24; MD + Aya: N = 23. For Fig. 3B: Control+Water: N = 23; MD+Water: N = 22; Control + Aya: N = 24; MD + Aya: N = 23

outcomes.summary: Ayahuasca did not alter square crossings. Rearing showed main effects of treatment (reduction) and MD, with no interaction and no significant post-hoc differences. The authors interpret this as a modest effect.
outcomes.evidence: Two-way ANOVA analysis on the number of square crossings identified no statistically significant differences

B1_num_measures.evidence: The frequency of crossings over the black lines and the count of rearings were recorded

B4_ethological.evidence: count of rearings — natural exploratory act scored as a distinct behaviour

B7_automated_classification.evidence: direct observation of the animals by the experimenter during real-time behavioral scoring

E1_environment_type.evidence: open area measuring 40 × 60 cm, surrounded by 4 walls

E3_bedding.evidence: The floor of the open area was divided into 9 equal squares indicated by black lines (no bedding described).

E6_spatial.evidence: open field with drawn squares only

D1_continuity.evidence: explore the space freely for 5 min

D5_followup.evidence: The open field test was performed 11 days after Ayahuasca administration.

assays.assay_description: Immediately after the OFT, in the same apparatus, 10% sucrose was sprayed on the dorsal coat. Grooming time was then observed for 5 min, 11 days after a single oral ayahuasca dose.

application_type.evidence: intragastric dose of Ayahuasca by oral gavage

setup_habituation.evidence: This period also served as the habituation phase for the splash test; therefore, no additional habituation period was provided.

setup_restrain.evidence: immediately returned to the upper left section of the apparatus for a further 5-min observation period

time_to_assay.evidence: The splash test was performed 11 days after Ayahuasca administration, immediately following the open field test.

sample_size.evidence: For Fig. 4: Control+Water: N = 22; MD+Water: N = 23; Control + Aya: N = 21; MD + Aya: N = 21.

outcomes.summary: Maternal deprivation reduced grooming time. A single ayahuasca dose restored grooming in MD rats. No Sex × Treatment interaction was found.
outcomes.evidence: However, Ayahuasca treatment reversed this effect in the Maternal Deprivation group (P < 0.0001).

E1_environment_type.evidence: Both tests were conducted sequentially in the same apparatus.

E3_bedding.evidence: Same open field; no bedding described.

D5_followup.evidence: The splash test was performed 11 days after Ayahuasca administration

assays.assay_description: 15-min pre-swim (training) on day 12, followed by a 5-min test on day 13 after a single oral ayahuasca dose. The test used a Plexiglas cylinder (50 cm high, 25 cm diameter) with 23 °C water. Immobility and climbing time were scored manually in the test session.

application_type.evidence: intragastric dose of Ayahuasca by oral gavage

setup_habituation.evidence: On the first day (training phase), rats were placed in a transparent Plexiglas cylinder ... for 15 min.

setup_restrain.evidence: rats were placed in a transparent Plexiglas cylinder (FST cylinder per rubric)

water_restriction.evidence: No drinking water source in cylinder

time_to_assay.evidence: The forced swim test was performed over 2 days (12 and 13 days after Ayahuasca administration); test phase day 13.

sample_size.evidence: For Fig. 5A: Control+Water: N = 22; MD+Water: N = 23; Control + Aya: N = 21; MD + Aya: N = 22. For Fig. 5B: Control+Water: N = 21; MD+Water: N = 20; Control + Aya: N = 24; MD + Aya: N = 21.

outcomes.summary: Maternal deprivation reduced climbing time, and a single ayahuasca dose restored climbing in MD rats. Immobility showed only an MD main effect; ayahuasca had no effect on immobility.
outcomes.evidence: Even so, Ayahuasca treatment reversed this effect in the Maternal Deprivation group (P < 0.0001).

B1_num_measures.evidence: The duration of immobility and climbing behavior (seconds) was measured manually ... Swimming behavior was not quantified separately

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility/climbing are not ethological per rubric.

E1_environment_type.evidence: transparent Plexiglas cylinder (height: 50 cm, diameter: 25 cm)

D1_continuity.evidence: Only the 5-min test phase data were analysed; training-phase data were not reported.

D2_session_duration.evidence: On the second day (test phase), rats were placed again in the same cylinder for 5 min.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Data reported from test day (13 days post-dose) only

D5_followup.evidence: The forced swim test was performed over 2 days (12 and 13 days after Ayahuasca administration).

judge_notes: All three candidates identified the same four behavioural assays (EPM, OFT, splash test, FST). Biochemical assays (ELISA, UHPLC-MS, oxidative stress) were excluded as non-behavioural.

D5_followup set to Yes (1) for all assays, overriding the 2/3 modal 'No'. Each test was run 10–13 days after a single dose, which satisfies the rubric's ≥24 h criterion; deepseek4's scoring matches the paper.
time_to_assay set to long_term_over7d. gemma4's short_term_1to7d is wrong for 10–13 day delays.

FST: the 15-min training swim was not scored or reported, so it is treated as apparatus habituation (setup_habituation=yes). D1/D2/D3 are based on the 5-min test only. gemma4's Multiple/15–60 min/2-day scoring was rejected.
FST B1 set to 1 (2 measures: immobility and climbing), correcting gemma4's score of 2. OFT B1=1 and splash B1=0 likewise correct gemma4's score/value mismatches. EPM B1=2 (4 reported measures).
OFT B4 set to Yes, overriding the 2/3 modal 'No'. Rearing is a natural exploratory act scored as a distinct behaviour, which the rubric explicitly includes; confidence is medium.
day_night_flipped is not_reported because the paper gives only a bare '12-hour light-dark cycle' (2/3 candidates agree).

Dosing vehicle recorded as water (control was intragastric water at 2 mL/kg; the brew is aqueous), with medium confidence. Total alkaloid dose of 10.62 mg/kg is used; per-alkaloid doses are listed in doses_raw.
Sample sizes follow modal values: EPM/OFT n_total=96 as designed, splash=87 and FST=88 as analysed after ROUT exclusions.
